[1/2] Charge wall-clock hides that span pause/reveal into the next timed board

impact_assessment.why: A timed run that hides during the 680ms post-correct pause or the 1150ms timeout reveal starts the next board while hidden; the hide handler records hiddenAt only in phase play, so returning charges nothing. Reproduced: 3.7s hidden, next board still 15000ms, full run scored 5580.
impact_assessment.benefits: Hiding at any point in an active timed run charges wall-clock time to the board the player returns to, closing the pause/reveal clock dodge while menu/result hides stay free.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: timer charging only, no scoring/script/storage changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the pending charge applies once on the next play frame; state: two transient run fields reset on start/quit/result.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure and shell-contract tests; real Chromium probe with 3.0s hidden during the pause; same 10-board played run; full gates.

[1/2] Record the outcome when Quit run lands on a decided timed run (loss reveal or last board pause)

impact_assessment.why: Quit run is enabled during the 1150ms fatal/timeout reveal and the 680ms post-final-pick pause. The run is already decided there (lives 0 or all boards cleared), but quitRun only adds abandoned totals, so the daily result, streak and win are erased. Reproduced: daily one clear plus three wrong picks, quit during the reveal, raw afterimage.daily stayed null and the menu read 'A fresh seeded set'.
impact_assessment.benefits: A decided run always lands on its result screen with the daily record, streak and win awards intact, so the 1.1s beat can no longer erase a loss or a cleared daily.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: quit routing only, no scoring/script/storage-schema changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the queued finish callback is neutralized by runId; state: no new saved fields.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure outcome test plus a quit-routing shell contract; real Chromium probe for the loss beat and the final-board pause; full gates.

[1/2] Keep keyboard focus on the same cell when a resize rebuilds the grid

impact_assessment.why: computeLayout() empties #cells and rebuilds every tile button, which destroys the focused element. The ResizeObserver fires ~60ms after a board starts and on every resize, so the board loses focus to BODY and arrows/Enter stop working. Reproduced: focus on cell 0 at board start, BODY after layout, then Enter and ArrowRight leave attempts at 0.
impact_assessment.benefits: Keyboard players keep their cell across the initial layout pass and any window resize, so arrow/Enter play works throughout a run instead of only in the first 60ms.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: focus restoration only, no scoring/layout/state changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the rebuild is synchronous; state: none new saved.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure index test plus a layout shell contract; real Chromium probe before/after for start-of-board and resize; full gates.

[1/2] Never claim a best, daily or profile change that a failed write did not persist

impact_assessment.why: store.set swallows localStorage failures, so saveBest/saveDaily/saveProfile report success while nothing is stored. With quota-denied writes a full Focus win showed NEW BEST and state.bests.focus 5580; after reload the menu had no best and EYE LV 1 - 0 clears - 0 runs. Reduced-motion and 320x568 layouts were probed and are clean dead ends.
impact_assessment.benefits: Result badges, daily records, freezes, first-clear callouts and lifetime stats are only claimed when the write actually lands, matching the blocked-key guarantees from ADR-035/036/037.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: persistence honesty only, no scoring/script/schema changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: rejected writes revert in-memory values to their prior shape.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first harness tests with a throwing storage for best/daily/profile; real Chromium quota probe before/after; full gates.

[1/2] Decide a timeout only when it spends the last life

impact_assessment.why: Cycle 32 set pendingOutcome to loss on every timeout, but a timeout that leaves a life keeps the run alive. Quitting inside that reveal recorded a FOCUS LOST result (0/10) instead of abandoning the attempt. Reproduced: Focus timeout at lives 2 with pending loss, quit produced won false cleared 0.
impact_assessment.benefits: A non-fatal timeout quits back to the menu and keeps one abandoned run, while a last-life timeout still records its loss with the red board.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: timeout outcome only, no scoring/timer/save changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the reveal timer still advances a live board; state: pendingOutcome empty for a live run.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure outcome test plus a shell contract forbidding the unconditional assignment; real Chromium probes for both the non-fatal and fatal paths; full gates.

[1/2] Never finish a timed run as a win when the final board was not cleared

impact_assessment.why: timeout() runs after pushing a red board and then calls advance(); advance() bumps the level and calls finish(true) whenever level >= levels.length. Timing out on the last board therefore records won true. Reproduced on Daily: 9 clears + a final timeout produced DAILY #312 COMPLETE, won true, 9/10, streak 1, wins.daily 1 and a NEW DAILY BEST.
impact_assessment.benefits: A last-board timeout ends as a loss, so the daily result, streak, first-clear award and best are never minted from an uncleared board.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: advance/finish outcome only, no scoring/script/schema changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the reveal timer still finishes once; state: daily.result won now matches the board strip.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure advance-outcome test plus a shell contract; real Chromium probe for the final-board timeout and a replay win; full gates.
